# host_mac_permission (Resource)

Declares a macOS privacy permission an application needs, and verifies whether it is granted.

macOS grants a Privacy & Security permission only through an explicit user action in System Settings or through a user-approved MDM profile. No supported interface grants one from a script, and the privacy database is protected by the same mechanism it records. **This resource never grants a permission.** It makes the dependency explicit in the configuration, reports the current state when the privacy database is readable, and names the exact pane and URL that grants it.

Use it to keep a permission that an application genuinely needs, such as Accessibility for Hammerspoon or Input Monitoring for Karabiner-Elements, next to the resource that installs that application.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "host_mac_permission" "hammerspoon_accessibility" {
  service = "accessibility"
  client  = "org.hammerspoon.Hammerspoon"
}

resource "host_mac_permission" "karabiner_input_monitoring" {
  service = "input_monitoring"
  client  = "org.pqrs.Karabiner-Elements.Settings"

  # Report a missing grant instead of failing the apply, and open the pane that
  # grants it.
  required                   = false
  open_settings_when_missing = true
}
```

## Reading the Permission State

`state` reports what macOS records:

| `state` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `granted` | The permission is in place. |
| `denied` | The user explicitly denied it. |
| `missing` | macOS has no decision recorded for this client. |
| `unknown` | The privacy database could not be read. |

Reading the privacy database requires Full Disk Access for the application that runs Terraform, usually the terminal. Without it every permission reports `unknown`. An `unknown` state is always a warning and never fails an apply, because Terraform cannot distinguish a missing permission from a permission it is not allowed to see. `denied` and `missing` fail the apply while `required` is true.

## Services

Name a service with a short name, or with the raw `kTCCService…` identifier macOS stores. Accessibility, Input Monitoring, Screen Recording, Full Disk Access, Developer Tools, and Bluetooth live in the system privacy database; every other service lives in the per-user one.

## Destroy Behavior

Destroying the resource changes nothing by default. Set `revoke_on_destroy = true` to run `tccutil reset` for this service and client, which returns the permission to its undecided state and makes the application ask again. `tccutil` only accepts a bundle identifier, so `revoke_on_destroy` cannot be used with a path `client`.

## Import

Import an existing declaration with `<service>:<client>`:

```shell
terraform import host_mac_permission.hammerspoon_accessibility 'accessibility:org.hammerspoon.Hammerspoon'
```

## Schema

### Required

- `client` (String) Bundle identifier such as `org.hammerspoon.Hammerspoon`, or the absolute path of a command-line executable.
- `service` (String) Privacy service to check. Use a short name such as `accessibility`, `input_monitoring`, `screen_recording`, or `full_disk_access`, or a raw `kTCCService…` identifier. Supported short names: `accessibility`, `automation`, `bluetooth`, `calendars`, `camera`, `contacts`, `desktop_folder`, `developer_tools`, `documents_folder`, `downloads_folder`, `full_disk_access`, `input_monitoring`, `media_library`, `microphone`, `photos`, `reminders`, `removable_volumes`, `screen_recording`, `speech_recognition`.

### Optional

- `open_settings_when_missing` (Boolean) Open the System Settings pane that grants this permission whenever it is not confirmed granted. Defaults to false.
- `required` (Boolean) Fail the apply when the permission is confirmed missing or denied. A state that cannot be read is always reported as a warning, never an error. Defaults to true.
- `revoke_on_destroy` (Boolean) Run `tccutil reset` for this service and client on destroy, returning the permission to its undecided state. Requires a bundle identifier `client`. Defaults to false.

### Read-Only

- `client_type` (String) How macOS identifies the client, either `bundle_id` or `path`, derived from `client`.
- `granted` (Boolean) True only when the permission was read and is granted.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier derived from `service` and `client`.
- `settings_url` (String) System Settings URL that opens the pane granting this permission.
- `state` (String) Observed permission state: `granted`, `denied`, `missing` when macOS has no decision recorded, or `unknown` when the privacy database cannot be read.
